chunks: Sahl, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is not befitting for anyone to sit with bent knees and arms around it, facing the Ka'bah.

key_terms.يَحْتَبِي: To sit with knees bent and arms wrapped around them

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on sitting in front of the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the etiquette (*adab*) of reverence towards the Ka'bah, prohibiting the casual posture of *ihtibay* (sitting with knees drawn up) directly facing it, which was considered too informal for such a sacred space. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the distinction between general respect and the specific decorum required in the presence of the House of Allah, reflecting the broader principle of honoring holy sites through dignified conduct.
